question: Can an LLM-guided program search improve its own sampling and refinement operators from execution traces and hindsight relabeling, rather than only spending more inference compute with a fixed model?

key_findings.claim: SOAR closes a search–learning loop around two learned operators: unconstrained Python sampling and execution-feedback-conditioned refinement.
key_findings.evidence: For each ARC task, the search samples 3,000 programs, executes them, then allocates 3,000 refinements with a REX Thompson-sampling/exploration policy. Programs are grouped by predicted test grid and weighted by demonstration accuracy for two-output voting. After search, LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning improves the same model's sampling and refinement behavior for the next iteration.

key_findings.claim: Hindsight relabeling converts every executable failed candidate into supervised data, but its validity is synthetic-task validity rather than progress on the original task.
key_findings.evidence: A sampled program f is relabeled as correct for the new mapping x -> f(x), producing 2.4 million potential rows across 400 training tasks before subsampling at most 50 per task. The greedy-diverse policy mixes 25 high-scoring and 25 low-scoring programs. This solves sparse feedback and expands data, but can train arbitrary or trivial transformations; program length preferences and filtering of hard-coded transduction are extra safeguards rather than guarantees of semantic usefulness.

anchors.section: F Program synthesis using a mix of induction and transduction

key_findings.claim: Ablations support learning both generation and repair rather than merely replaying more samples.
key_findings.evidence: On ARC-train with Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B, greedy-diverse sampling fine-tuning reaches 36.46% solved versus 29.67% without fine-tuning. Diverse refinement training raises Sample&Refine from 34.83% to 42.88%. Jointly fine-tuning both roles yields 39.79% sampling and 44.42% search, exceeding the separate-role configurations. A FLOP-matched 12,600-attempt fixed-model baseline remains below one learned generation in Appendix B.

anchors.section: E Learning to generate and refine jointly / Table 7

key_findings.claim: The 52% headline is a high-compute cross-model ensemble on the public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set, not a single self-improved model score.
key_findings.evidence: Individual SOAR scores after train- and test-time iterations range from 36.25% for Qwen-Coder-7B to 45.50% for Mistral-Large-2. The 52.00% result combines five model sizes with weighted majority voting at 6,000 attempts each; the oracle over generated outputs is 57.25%. The paper reports 30,000 attempts per task for the ensemble and four training plus two test-time learning iterations, so comparisons with one-shot closed models or lower-budget systems are capability/context comparisons, not compute-equivalent leaderboards.

key_findings.claim: The loop improves on this benchmark but shows early symptoms of self-generated-data collapse rather than evidence of open-ended improvement.
key_findings.evidence: Solution embedding diversity steadily decreases on solved tasks and falls then plateaus on unsolved tasks; performance gains diminish across iterations. The authors explicitly identify low diversity, 6,000 attempts per task per iteration, and ARC-only evaluation as limits, and propose quality-diversity or new-problem generation. No prospective scaling law, held-out ARC-AGI-2 result, or cross-domain transfer test demonstrates that further iterations continue to add capability.

method.core_idea: Internalize successful and failed evolutionary-search experience into the LLM so that later search uses better proposal and mutation/refinement operators.
method.mechanism: Execute 3,000 sampled Python programs and 3,000 bandit-allocated refinements per task; construct supervised sampling examples by hindsight relabeling and refinement examples from successful repairs; repeatedly fine-tune a base model on selected archive data; optionally adapt sampling on unlabeled test tasks using demonstration accuracy and weighted-output groups.
assumptions: Execution on a sandboxed ARC interpreter supplies a trustworthy and sufficiently dense evaluator.
Relabeled mappings preserve transferable program structure rather than mostly teaching arbitrary self-generated tasks.
Training-pair accuracy and output-frequency voting correlate with correctness on the hidden test grid.
The public ARC evaluation tasks and base-model pretraining do not introduce material contamination or benchmark-specific overfitting.
Compute comparisons can be normalized adequately with approximate forward/backward FLOP accounting.

techniques.role: Uses an LLM as both initial program generator and semantics-aware mutation/refinement operator.
Turns failed candidates into valid synthetic task–program supervision.
Allocates a fixed refinement budget between promising lineages and exploration.
Retrains search operators from the accumulated program archive.
Selects two predicted grids from many programs without test labels.

evaluations.result: sampling rises from 29.67% to 36.46%; refinement-trained search rises from 34.83% to 42.88%; joint training reaches 44.42% search
evaluations.baseline: same 3k/6k search budgets with the non-fine-tuned or separately fine-tuned model

evaluations.setting: ARC public evaluation set across 7B–123B open models
evaluations.result: individual final SOAR models score 36.25%–45.50%; five-model weighted ensemble scores 52.00%, oracle 57.25%
evaluations.baseline: fixed Sample&Refine-6k scores 14.25%–26.25% and one-shot scores 1.00%–2.50% for the same open-model families

evaluations.setting: Two unlabeled test-time training iterations after four ARC-train iterations
evaluations.result: approximately +5 points overall; Qwen-Coder-7B moves from initial 14.25% fixed search to 36.25% final SOAR

evaluations.setting: FLOP-matched search scaling for the 7B model
evaluations.result: one learned SOAR generation outperforms 12,600 fixed-model attempts at the estimated same FLOPs
evaluations.baseline: Sample&Refine with the base model and extra samples

limitations: Only ARC-AGI-1 is evaluated; domain-agnostic or ARC-AGI-2 transfer is not demonstrated.
The 52% headline pools five models and roughly 30,000 attempts per task, obscuring the single-model/compute frontier.
Evaluation uses the public test set, making contamination and repeated design-selection concerns harder to exclude than on a private holdout.
Self-generated solution diversity declines and gains diminish across iterations.
Hindsight tasks are correct by construction but may be uninformative, degenerate, or reward easy-to-copy transformations.
The paper reports approximate FLOPs but not total wall-clock, energy, or repeated-seed variability for the full system.
failure_modes: Majority voting can amplify a common brittle or hard-coded program family even when a rare candidate is correct.
Fine-tuning on self-generated mappings can narrow the mutation distribution and trap search in structural attractors.
Execution-based fitness over a few demonstrations permits overfitting and accidental test-grid errors.
Unsafe generated Python can escape or exhaust an insufficiently isolated evaluator.
Test-time self-training can reinforce pseudo-label errors because hidden outputs provide no correction signal.
reusable_insights: Compare learning-to-search against FLOP-matched extra search, not only against equal candidate counts.
Separate generation-bound, refinement-bound, and selection-bound errors with oracle candidate analysis.
Failed programs become useful data when goals can be relabeled exactly by execution, but synthetic-task quality must still be measured.
Track behavioral and structural diversity prospectively across self-improvement generations.
Use cross-model archives when they add complementary solutions, but report ensemble and single-model frontiers separately.
open_questions: Does SOAR improve on ARC-AGI-2 or unseen program-synthesis domains without benchmark-specific redesign?
Which hindsight-generated tasks predict improvement on original held-out tasks, and can low-value relabels be filtered prospectively?
Can quality-diversity archives prevent mutation collapse while retaining the sample-efficiency gains of fine-tuning?
How many self-improvement generations remain beneficial under a fixed total compute budget?
Can a calibrated verifier close the 5.25-point ensemble-to-oracle gap without test-label leakage?
What sandbox and resource controls are sufficient when transferring the loop from grids to general software?

competitive_landscape.title: CodeIt: Self-Improving Language Models with Prioritized Hindsight Replay
competitive_landscape.difference: CodeIt already alternates ARC program sampling, hindsight relabeling, and prioritized replay in a hand-designed DSL; SOAR moves to general Python, adds explicit execution-guided iterative refinement, joint operator training, larger code models, and test-time adaptation.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv record and ICML 2024 proceedings checked 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: Mathematical Discoveries from Program Search with Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: FunSearch evolves scored program components with a fixed LLM and island archive for mathematical/algorithmic objectives; SOAR fine-tunes its proposal/refinement model from traces and targets few-example ARC transformations.

competitive_landscape.title: AlphaEvolve: A Coding Agent for Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: AlphaEvolve orchestrates strong fixed LLMs, evaluators, and an evolutionary database across scientific and infrastructure problems; SOAR's differentiator is weight adaptation of both sampling and refinement operators from hindsight traces.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolution through Large Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ELM couples LLM mutation with MAP-Elites and then trains a conditional generator from evolved artifacts; SOAR repeatedly trains the search operators themselves, but lacks ELM's explicit quality-diversity archive.

competitive_landscape.title: Mutation Without Variation: Convergence Dynamics in LLM-Driven Program Evolution
competitive_landscape.difference: Gurkan et al. isolate LLM mutation without selection and find strong structural attractors and revisitation; it sharpens SOAR's observed diversity decline into a concrete risk that learned semantic mutation can collapse unless variation is explicitly protected.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: SOAR is a self-improving evolutionary program-synthesis framework that learns both sampling and refinement from its own traces and reaches 52% on the ARC-AGI public test set.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper provides operator-learning ablations, four train-time and two test-time iterations over several model scales, FLOP-matched extra-search comparisons, archive aggregation, and diversity measurements.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The joint refinement/sampling training and unlabeled test-time continuation are meaningful extensions of CodeIt and fixed-model evolutionary search. The result is strong evidence for learning-to-search on ARC, but not yet for open-ended self-improvement: the headline is an expensive public-set ensemble, diversity narrows, and no new domain or private benchmark tests scaling.

reviewer_notes: Read the full 32-page ICML paper including algorithms, compute-matched appendix, data-selection details, and transduction safeguards. The competitive panel was updated through 2026-08-23 using primary arXiv, PMLR, and Nature records, including a later study of LLM mutation collapse.
